seeds.name: Convert CSV to JSON
seeds.description: A 2,000-row block repeated 30 times (60,000 rows) converted record-by-record to JSON; about 78-110ms, exercising mlr's format-conversion hot path. Conversion is row-independent, so the repeated block measures the same work a distinct table would.

seeds.name: Grouped statistics by department
seeds.description: A 2,000-row block repeated 35 times (70,000 rows) aggregated into five statistics per department (8 groups, from the block's id%8 department cycle); about 60-70ms, exercising stats1's streaming accumulator path. The group key is the low-cardinality department code, not the row id, so the repeated block does not change what is measured.

seeds.name: Numeric sort descending
seeds.description: A 2,000-row block repeated 30 times (60,000 rows) sorted numerically descending on one column; about 55-60ms, the most expensive of the five seeds. Sort does not care about row uniqueness.

seeds.name: Filter by a DSL boolean expression
seeds.description: A 2,000-row block repeated 35 times (70,000 rows) filtered by a DSL boolean expression on one column; about 29-33ms, exercising mlr's filter-expression evaluator. Filtering is row-independent.

seeds.name: Compute a derived column with the put DSL
seeds.description: A 2,000-row block repeated 30 times (60,000 rows) with a new column computed by a put DSL expression; about 32-34ms, exercising mlr's put evaluator. Evaluation is row-independent.

seeds.name: Numeric sort at stress scale
seeds.description: The same 2,000-row block (repeated 30 times to reconstruct a 60,000-row fixture) given 45 times as separate positional arguments (mlr concatenates multi-file input), about 3.7s on this machine, without inflating the manifest with a second large fixture.
